## Pedigree as genetic information

Two full siblings share, on average, 50% of their genes. Two paternal half-siblings share 25%. This degree of genetic relatedness — expressed as **relatedness coefficient (a_ij)** — is the basis for connecting assessments of animals in different herds and times.

The **Numerical Relationship Matrix (A)**, also called the Numerator Relationship Matrix, organizes these coefficients:

- **Diagonal:** a_ii = 1 + F_i (where F_i = inbreeding coefficient of animal i)
- **Off-diagonal:** a_ij = 2 × θ_ij (twice the relationship coefficient between i and j)

::: {.callout-note}
**Central concept:** The diagonal of A is not simply "1" for everyone. For an inbred animal (related parents), a_ii = 1 + F_i > 1. This reflects that its two alleles are more likely to be identical by descent (IBD).
:::

## Expected values ​​of a_ij

| Relationship | a_ij |
|---|---|
| Animal with itself (no inbreeding) | 1.0 |
| Father–son | 0.5 |
| Full siblings (no inbreeding) | 0.5 |
| Paternal half-siblings (no inbreeding) | 0.25 |
| Grandfather–grandson | 0.25 |
| Cousins ​​| 0.125 |
| Unrelated animals | 0.0 |

## Henderson's tabular method

```r
#| label: constroi-A
# Pedigree de 10 animais (ordem cronológica obrigatória)
ped <- data.frame(
  animal = 1:10,
  sire   = c(0,0,0, 1,1, 4,4, 6,6, 8),
  dam    = c(0,0,0, 2,3, 5,5, 5,7, 7)
)
cat("=== Pedigree ===\n"); print(ped)

# Método tabular: constrói A linha por linha
n <- nrow(ped)
A <- matrix(0, n, n)

for (i in 1:n) {
  s <- ped$sire[i]; d <- ped$dam[i]
  # Diagonal
  A[i,i] <- if (s==0 || d==0) 1 else 1 + 0.5*A[s,d]
  # Off-diagonal (j < i)
  for (j in seq_len(i-1)) {
    A[j,i] <- A[i,j] <- if (s==0 && d==0) 0
                          else if (s==0)   0.5*A[j,d]
                          else if (d==0)   0.5*A[j,s]
                          else             0.5*(A[j,s]+A[j,d])
  }
}
```

```r
#| label: interpreta-A
cat("=== Matriz A (arredondada) ===\n")
print(round(A, 4))

Fi <- diag(A) - 1
cat("\n=== Coeficientes de endogamia (F_i) ===\n")
for (i in 1:n)
  if (Fi[i] > 0) cat(sprintf("Animal %2d: F = %.4f (pais: %d × %d)\n",
                              i, Fi[i], ped$sire[i], ped$dam[i]))
if (all(Fi == 0)) cat("Nenhum animal endogâmico neste pedigree.\n")
```

```r
#| label: verifica-parentescos
cat("=== Verificação de coeficientes de parentesco ===\n")
pares <- list(
  list(i=4,  j=5,  relacao="Irmãos completos (pai 1, mãe 2/3 distintas)"),
  list(i=6,  j=7,  relacao="Irmãos completos (pai 4, mãe 5)"),
  list(i=4,  j=6,  relacao="Pai (4) – filho (6)"),
  list(i=1,  j=6,  relacao="Avô (1) – neto (6)"),
  list(i=1,  j=2,  relacao="Fundadores não aparentados"),
  list(i=8,  j=9,  relacao="Irmãos completos (pai 6, mãe 5/7)")
)
for (p in pares)
  cat(sprintf("a[%d,%d] = %.4f  ← %s\n", p$i, p$j, A[p$i,p$j], p$relacao))
```

```r
#| label: inversa-A
cat("\n=== Inversa de A (5×5 primeiros) ===\n")
Ainv <- solve(A)
print(round(Ainv[1:5,1:5], 4))
cat("\n(Valores fora da diagonal de A⁻¹ conectam parentes nas MME)\n")
```

```r
#| label: media-endogamia-geracoes
cat("\n=== Coeficiente médio de parentesco (diagonal média de A) ===\n")
for (g in list(1:3, 4:5, 6:7, 8:9, 10)) {
  cat(sprintf("Geração (~%s): diagonal média = %.4f\n",
              paste(g, collapse="-"), mean(diag(A)[g])))
}
```

## Interpretation

- Animals 4 and 5 (children of 1 × 2 and 1 × 3, respectively) have a[4,5] ≈ 0.25 — half-siblings, not full siblings, because they have different mothers.
- The diagonals of the first generation (founders) are all 1.0; in subsequent generations, they can exceed 1.0 if there is inbreeding.
- A⁻¹ has a crucial property: it is **sparse** (many zeros), which makes the MME system computationally efficient even with millions of animals.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Attention:** The pedigree must be ordered chronologically — parents before children. An out-of-order animal produces silent errors in matrix A.
:::

## Proposed exercise

1. Add to the pedigree an animal 11 with `sire=4` and `dam=5` (brother crossed with sister). Calculate F_11.
2. What happens to the diagonal of A if all animals are father × daughter repeatedly for 3 generations?
3. Compare `solve(A)` with `solve(A + 0.01*diag(n))`. Why does regularization help?
